title: Staying on DDR4 in 2026: The Best DDR4 Upgrades for AM4 and Intel PCs
summary: Staying on AM4 or a DDR4 Intel board? Why a matched 32GB DDR4 kit is the smart upgrade in 2026, plus the best DDR4-3200 and 3600 kits to buy.
body_markdown:
An r/buildapc thread asked something I've been hearing a lot in 2026: is it reasonable to stay on AM4 for another three or four years and wait for AM6? The poster's reasoning was simple. DDR5 prices made a platform switch hard to justify. Several of the top replies agreed. "Stay on AM4!" one wrote, pointing out that the Ryzen 5000 X3D chips are about as fast as non-X3D Ryzen 7000 parts in games.


I think that's the right call for a lot of people with an AM4 or Intel 12th to 14th Gen DDR4 system. But it changes what a smart upgrade looks like, and memory is usually the first place I'd look.


## Why DDR4 Upgrades Make Sense in 2026


The memory market has been rough. In July 2025, TrendForce News, citing Taiwan's Commercial Times, reported DDR4 end-of-life timelines for Samsung, Micron and SK hynix. Then AI demand pushed the whole DRAM market up. TrendForce forecast another 10 to 15 percent quarter-over-quarter rise in conventional DRAM contract prices for the fourth quarter of 2026, even as the pace of increases moderates. Micron even wound down its Crucial consumer business to focus on data center demand.


None of that makes DDR4 cheap. It does make a full platform change, with a new board, CPU and DDR5 kit, a much bigger bill than keeping your current board and fixing the weak spot.


## What to Look For in a DDR4 Kit


**Capacity: 32GB is my target.** One reply in that thread called 16GB "kinda the lower limit," and I agree. Going from 16GB to 32GB is the upgrade you'll notice in big open-world games, with browsers and Discord open in the background.


**Two sticks, not four.** AMD's official memory ratings for the Ryzen 7 5800X3D tell the story: DDR4-3200 with two modules, but 2933 with four single-rank modules and 2667 with four dual-rank modules. A fresh 2 x 16GB kit usually beats adding a second pair to your old 2 x 8GB.


**Don't mix kits if you can avoid it.** Even identical-looking sticks bought years apart can use different memory chips, and that's where instability starts.


**Speed: 3200 to 3600.** AMD rates Ryzen 5000 at DDR4-3200, and AMD itself used DDR4-3600 for its 5800X3D anniversary benchmarks. I'd stay in that range rather than chasing higher-rated kits. Intel's 12th, 13th and 14th Gen chips support DDR4 on DDR4 motherboards too, and the same advice applies.

## The Picks


### Best Overall: G.SKILL Ripjaws V 32GB DDR4-3600 CL16


The[G.SKILL Ripjaws V 32GB DDR4-3600](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820232907?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) kit runs 16-19-19-39 at 1.35V, and it has more than 8,000 ratings on Newegg. It's the default I'd recommend to almost anyone on AM4.


### Best With RGB: G.SKILL Trident Z Neo 32GB DDR4-3600 CL16


Same speed and timings as the Ripjaws V, plus RGB lighting, and the[G.SKILL Trident Z Neo](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820232861?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) is marketed specifically for Ryzen systems.


### Best for Big Air Coolers: CORSAIR Vengeance LPX 32GB DDR4-3200


If your CPU cooler overhangs the memory slots, the low-profile[CORSAIR Vengeance LPX](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820236541?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) is the safe fit at DDR4-3200 CL16. The[Team T-FORCE VULCAN Z 32GB DDR4-3200](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820331618?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) is a similar no-frills alternative.


### For Creators: 64GB Kits


If you edit video or run virtual machines, 64GB in two sticks is the clean way to get there. AMD's rating for two dual-rank sticks is DDR4-3200, so I'd start with the[Kingston FURY Beast RGB 64GB DDR4-3200 CL16](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820242806?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) or the[Patriot Viper Steel 64GB DDR4-3200](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820225208?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) . The[Kingston FURY Beast 64GB DDR4-3600](https://www.newegg.com/p/0RN-001J-01081?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) kit is rated faster, and 3600 often works with two 32GB sticks, but it isn't guaranteed.


## If You Also Want a CPU Upgrade


AMD brought back the[Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113940?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) on June 25, 2026: eight cores, 96MB of L3 cache and a 105W TDP, still on AM4 and DDR4. It doesn't include a cooler. AMD's Travis Kirsch called the re-release "a final gift to our loyal users," a nod to long-time AM4 owners. AMD hasn't announced further AM4 chips. We covered the relaunch in more detail in[our look at the 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition](https://www.newegg.com/insider/amd-ryzen-7-5800x3d-is-back-10th-anniversary-edition-returns-to-newegg/?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-ddr4-ram-upgrades-am4-intel-2026) . Update your BIOS before you swap chips.


## Final Verdict


If you're on AM4 with 16GB, a matched 32GB DDR4-3600 kit is the best value upgrade you can make, and the Ripjaws V is the one I'd buy. Add the 5800X3D if your CPU is the bottleneck. Then let AM5 and DDR5 prices settle while your current PC keeps doing its job.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is it worth staying on AM4 in 2026?** For many gamers, yes. With DDR5 and platform costs high, keeping an AM4 board and upgrading memory or moving to a Ryzen 5000 X3D chip is far cheaper than switching to AM5, and AMD re-released the Ryzen 7 5800X3D in June 2026.


**How much DDR4 RAM do I need for gaming in 2026?** 32GB is the practical target. 16GB still runs most games, but it leaves little headroom once you add a browser, Discord and other background apps.


**Is DDR4-3600 better than DDR4-3200 for Ryzen?** AMD officially rates Ryzen 5000 chips like the 5800X3D at DDR4-3200 with two modules, and AMD used DDR4-3600 in its own 5800X3D anniversary benchmarks. Either is a sensible choice; I'd buy a 3600 CL16 kit for 2 x 16GB and 3200 for 2 x 32GB.


**Should I use two or four sticks of DDR4?** Two. AMD's 5800X3D ratings drop from DDR4-3200 with two modules to 2933 with four single-rank modules and 2667 with four dual-rank modules, so a 2 x 16GB kit is better than adding a second pair.


**Can I mix my old DDR4 kit with a new one?** It may work, but it's a common source of instability because modules bought at different times can use different memory chips. A single matched kit is the safer route.
